acceptanceClaims: one disposable Windows KVM Guest remained in the same QEMU lifecycle while lightweight peer A was removed and lightweight peer B was introduced
Host Linux netlink/bridge observations independently retained the exact peer-a-present, peer-a-removed, and peer-b-present topology sequence
the final current fabric truth points to peer B rather than retaining the stale initial peer-A snapshot
the maintained Guest canary completed distinct TCP interactions with peer A and peer B without requesting external network access
the Host tcpdump sensor independently observed both maintained TCP exchanges without being promoted to world truth
QEMU, swtpm, the disposable Run directory, root-owned ledger, fabric namespace, and surviving replacement-peer namespace all closed without declared residuals

sensor: Host tcpdump observation of peer-A and peer-B traffic
worldTruth: Host Linux netlink/bridge peer-A-removed intermediate snapshot
Host Linux netlink/bridge peer-B-present snapshot and current fabric truth

falsifiers.failure: the first replacement-peer readiness check classified any process that had already exited after 250 ms as startup failure; in a live world an already-running Guest can consume the one-shot peer fast enough for exit 0 to represent successful service completion

a physical run completed both flows and emitted topology history, but inherited current fabricTruth remained the initial peer-A snapshot; S6 then required current truth and historical truth to remain consistent
the corrected dirty-tree candidate retained the exact three topology phases and final peer-B current truth before the implementation was committed for exact-revision acceptance

limitations: the topology change is management-driven rather than requested by an evaluated Actor
S6 uses one full Windows Guest and sequential maintained lightweight peers rather than several full-OS failure domains
the accepted topology is one unrouted L2 segment with no DHCP, DNS, NAT, routing, zones, or external egress
tcpdump remains a fallible external sensor and is not claimed to be complete world truth
S6 does not introduce a generic RangeNode, topology graph, materialization registry, world-mutation API, or action gateway
S6 does not admit unknown Samples, third-party malware, Internet egress, or external targets
